title: runtime-api-surface-draft
content:
Runtime API surface - draft

Authors: Maya Patel (owner), Ethan Chen, Priya Sharma
Status: Draft — feedback requested from serving-runtime, infra, and product-hosted-api
Last updated: 2025-02-20

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Define the runtime-facing API surface used by Redwood control plane (hosted/dedicated/private) and internal egress components to submit inference work. This doc focuses on the request/response schema, error semantics, versioning/compatibility guarantees, and interactions with kernels, scheduling, and KV cache.
- Scope: Request submission, streaming vs non-streaming, response envelope, deterministic error codes, contract for kernel selection hints and scheduling hints, and explicit KV cache usage. Not covered: user-facing SDKs, billing events, or observability payloads (those are separate schemas).

Goals
- Provide a stable, minimal request schema v1 that supports: chat (turned history), completion, embeddings, and reranking requests.
- Support streaming and chunked responses with unambiguous reassembly semantics.
- Define clear error categories and machine-friendly error codes.
- Allow runtime to accept hints for kernel/quantization preferences without changing request semantics. Hints are advisory; compatibility guarantees apply.
- Explicitly model KV cache references so control plane can perform cache warmup and reuse across requests.

Non-goals
- Not proposing final SDK naming or HTTP-level auth headers.
- Not encoding cost/billing tokens in this surface.

High-level design principles
- Backwards compatible: v1 -> v2 migration must be opt-in. New fields are optional; removal deprecated with 6-month notice.
- Hints-only approach: Kernel and scheduling hints must be best-effort; runtime may ignore if constraints differ.
- Deterministic error codes: Clients can implement robust retry/fallback strategies based on code families.
- Minimal coupling with C/C++ runtime internals — use string enums and IDs.

API Versioning and compatibility guarantees
- Schema versioning: request/response includes "runtime_api_version" header field (semantic string, e.g., "1"). Server must accept requests without this header (default to "1") for compatibility.
- Additive changes: adding optional fields does not break older clients.
- Removal or semantic changes: will be marked deprecated in the contract and rejected only when the client includes "runtime_api_version": "<new>".
- Backwards guarantees: For any accepted request, runtime must continue to produce semantically equivalent output for 12 months unless a critical bug fix requires behavior change; breaking fixes must be documented with migration notes.

Top-level request schema (v1) - JSON representation
- All fields listed here are strings, arrays of strings, or primitive types. The runtime accepts UTF-8.

Example request (completions/chat)
{
  "runtime_api_version": "1",
  "request_id": "req-20250210-8a7f",
  "model": "gpt-redwood-q4f",           // catalog model id
  "mode": "chat",                      // enum: chat | completion | embedding | rerank
  "priority": "normal",                // enum: low | normal | high  (scheduling hint)
  "kernel_hints": ["fast-attn-v2", "int8"], // advisory; runtime chooses best match
  "kv_cache_refs": ["cache:session-abc123", "cache:global-prefix-1"], // optional
  "prompt": [                             // chat/history array; each item is a single-turn object as stringified JSON for flexibility
    "{\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": \"You are a helpful assistant.\"}",
    "{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Summarize the following logs...\"}"
  ],
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "stream": true                         // boolean => streaming requested
}

Field descriptions (high level)
- runtime_api_version (optional): string
- request_id (required): client-assigned unique id for idempotency and tracing
- model (required): model catalog identifier
- mode (required): indicates expected semantic (chat/completion/embedding/rerank)
- priority (optional): scheduling hint. Low may be queued longer; high preferred for latency SLOs but charged accordingly.
- kernel_hints (optional): list of string tokens describing kernel/quantization preferences. Examples: "fast-attn-v2", "int8", "bf16-kernel". Runtime may map these to available kernels or ignore them.
- kv_cache_refs (optional): list of cache refs to attach. Control plane can pass session-level caches or precomputed prefixes. Cache refs are opaque strings resolved by runtime. If present runtime must attempt to lookup and use them for prefix generation.
- prompt (required for chat/completion/rerank): array of strings (each representing a role/content JSON). We intentionally use strings to avoid schema drift from evolving message types.
- max_tokens, temperature, top_p: numeric generation params
- stream: boolean; if true runtime should open a streaming channel (see streaming semantics)

Streaming semantics
- If stream=true, runtime responds with a streaming multipart channel (HTTP/2+gRPC streaming preferred). Each chunk must include: type (progress|delta|final|error), request_id, seq (incrementing integer), and payload (string).
- Reassembly: client should concatenate ordered delta chunks by seq to reconstruct incremental output. If connection drops, client may re-issue same request_id with a header "stream_resume": true; runtime may supply last_seq_ack to allow resuming from last acknowledged token if KV cache and policy permit. Resume is best-effort and not guaranteed across topology changes.

Response envelope (non-streaming)
{
  "request_id": "req-...",
  "status": "ok",            // ok | partial | error
  "model": "gpt-redwood-q4f",
  "generated_text": "...",
  "usage": {"input_tokens": "12", "output_tokens": "34"}, // strings to avoid numeric precision issues in some clients
  "kv_cache_written": ["cache:session-abc123"] // list of cache refs that runtime persisted as a result
}

Error model and canonical error codes
- Error envelope: {"request_id": "...", "status": "error", "error_code": "<code>", "message": "human readable"}
- Error code taxonomy (all codes are short strings):
  - transient/* : transient runtime conditions where retry may succeed (e.g., transient/resource-starved)
    - transient/resource_exhausted (GPUs busy, batching full)
    - transient/network (egress failure contacting upstream kv store)
  - policy/* : user request policy violations (do not retry without modification)
    - policy/unsupported_model
    - policy/invalid_prompt
    - policy/rate_limited
  - fatal/* : request cannot be fulfilled (non-retryable)
    - fatal/invalid_schema
    - fatal/model_mismatch (requested model not compatible with mode)
  - cache/* : KV cache related
    - cache/missing_ref (kv_cache_refs contained unknown ref)
    - cache/read_error (failed to read cache but may still process)
  - kernel/* : kernel selection/runtime incompatibility
    - kernel/no_compatible_kernel (requested kernel hints cannot be satisfied)

Retry guidance by code family
- transient/*: safe to retry with exponential backoff. Clients MAY lower priority on retry.
- policy/*: do not retry unchanged; surface to user for remediation.
- fatal/*: do not retry; client must surface.
- cache/read_error: runtime should continue best-effort; client may retry if cached prefixes are critical.

Idempotency and exactly-once considerations
- request_id is used for idempotency at the runtime submission layer. If the runtime receives a duplicate request_id within a retention window (default 60s) it should return cached response or a consensus status indicating duplicate.
- For long-running streaming requests a resumed request with same request_id and stream_resume=true is allowed and best-effort. Exactly-once generation is not guaranteed across network partitions.

Kernel and scheduling hints (contract)
- Hints are advisory. The runtime will attempt to match a kernel based on: model architecture, sequence length estimate (derived from prompt + max_tokens), and kernel_hints.
- Kernel fallback: if no kernel matches requested hints, runtime returns kernel/no_compatible_kernel with suggestion list in message OR silently fall back to a compatible kernel unless client supplied header "kernel_require": true; in that case runtime returns an error.
- Scheduling: priority hint affects queue ordering and preemption eligibility. "high" requests may be admitted into reserved fast lanes; "low" may be scheduled to batch windows or cheaper endpoints. Scheduler reserves the right to override priority for system stability.

KV cache contract and semantics
- KV cache refs are opaque strings. They represent either: session caches (per-conversation KV), prefix caches (precomputed embeddings/prefix states), or model-level constants. Runtime resolves them via configured cache backend (in-memory, redis, remote store).
- Read semantics: If a cache ref is provided, runtime must attempt to read it before generation. Read failures produce cache/read_error (transient) or cache/missing_ref (policy/fatal) depending on configured strictness flag per-tenant. If strictness="fail_on_missing" in request metadata, missing_ref is fatal.
- Write semantics: Runtime SHOULD expose which cache refs were written as "kv_cache_written" in the response envelope. Writes may be asynchronous; presence in kv_cache_written indicates persistence acknowledged.
- Consistency: No cross-instance consistency guarantees are provided by default. If strict consistency is required, control plane must provision co-located runtime instance or use Private deployment modes.

Observability hooks and metadata (brief)
- Requests include optional metadata map (string->string) for tracing (e.g., correlation ids). This metadata is opaque and persisted in traces/logs.
- Runtime must emit events with request_id, model, final status, error_code when errors occur. (Separate observability schema exists).

Examples and common flows
1) Low-latency chat: client sends priority=high, stream=true, kernel_hints=["fast-attn-v2"]. Runtime admits to fast lane, may ignore int8 hint if model not quantized; returns partial deltas quickly.
2) Batch embeddings: client sets mode=embedding, priority=low, stream=false. Scheduler batches multiple requests for throughput. Kernel_hints may include "embedding-opt".
3) Session reuse: Control plane sends kv_cache_refs for session id; runtime reads prefix, applies it, writes back new session ref on response. If cache missing and tenant strictness=best_effort, runtime proceeds but returns cache/missing_ref warning in response message and kv_cache_written=[] or updated refs.

Open questions / deferred items
- Exact format for metadata map and allowed keys for tenant-level strictness flags.
- Wire-level streaming protocol (HTTP chunked vs grpc) — recommend gRPC in Dedicated and Private, and HTTP2/Multipart for Hosted API gateway.
- Retry windows and idempotency window length per deployment mode.

Next steps / asks
- Feedback from infra and SRE: viability of resume semantics given current KV store topology.
- Product input on header names for kernel_require and stream_resume to align with SDKs.
- Security review for allowing opaque cache refs across shared tenancy.

Appendix: quick error code table
- transient/resource_exhausted => retry w/ backoff or lower max_tokens / priority
- transient/network => retry
- policy/invalid_prompt => surface to user, do not retry
- policy/unsupported_model => suggest models in message
- fatal/invalid_schema => client bug
- kernel/no_compatible_kernel => provide supported kernel list or accept fallback
- cache/missing_ref => depends on strictness; default: warning, proceed

This draft aims to balance a stable, minimal contract for runtime submission while providing knobs for performance tuning and cache reuse. Please add comments inline in this Drive doc or send PR to github:runtime/pull/456 for schema changes.
